title: Contact

reading.body:
The World of AI prioritizes factual accuracy above all other mail, with corrections updated to the live site within twenty-four hours of receipt.

This reflects a specific editorial choice. A site whose thesis depends on precise numbers about compute, power, and infrastructure cannot tolerate errors compounding across readers and citations. The correction workflow treats the data layer as a thing to be fixed at source rather than debated in comments or clarified in errata sections. That architecture matters because downstream claims about AI scaling constraints rest on accuracy in the underlying facts.

The site separates its atlas function from its consulting practice deliberately. One email reaches the publication itself. Another reaches a parent practice that does AI governance advisory work. This split lets readers distinguish between reference material and commercial engagement, and it signals that verdicts on the site are not for sale. The disclosure rules reinforce this. Advertising and sponsorship are permitted but labeled, and payment does not alter a ranking or a finding.

The site publishes its data through both human-readable pages and machine endpoints. It invites corrections, API requests for new fields, and press inquiries through labeled channels. It does not document what happens to suggestions that fall outside these categories, or how the publication prioritizes competing requests. Those limits aside, the contact structure is built to make the site verifiable and usable by other researchers and journalists working on the same questions.

sections.body: Two ways to reach us. For the atlas itself, corrections, data questions, press, write theworldofai@inkboxmail.com, which is the direct line to this publication. For the consulting practice, info@srjconsultingservices.com. We answer within one business day.

Use the subject line Correction and include the page URL and what is wrong. Corrections are the highest-priority mail we get. If a fact on this site is wrong, we fix it at the source and the fix publishes on the next daily run, usually within twenty-four hours.
Use the subject line API. Our public endpoints are documented at /api/. If you need a field we do not publish, ask; we would rather extend the endpoint than have you scrape the pages.

Use the subject line Press. Journalists and researchers are welcome to quote and cite this site. Every reference page carries a cite box with the URL and retrieval date. We can confirm methodology and point you to the primary sources behind any number we publish.
Use the subject line Advertising. Our rules are published in advance at Disclosure: everything paid is labeled, and no placement changes a verdict, a ranking, or a legal status.
AI governance advisory work is handled by our parent practice at srjconsultingservices.com.
